messages:
alex: seeing a bunch of errors from the inference fleet in ap-southeast-1 after the interface endpoint migration. apps can't reach external model registry (S3) — TLS handshake resets and then conn reset.
jen: noted. are the endpoints resolving to the interface IPs?
alex: yes DNS -> vpce-abc123.ap-southeast-1.vpce.amazonaws.com -> 10.0.58.21 (ENI)
raj: can you paste the curl error?
alex: here:
```
curl -v https://registry.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/healthcheck
* About to connect() to registry.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.0.58.21...
* Connected to 10.0.58.21 (10.0.58.21) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* TLS handshake completed, but then: 
* recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```
casey: that looks like ENI accepts TCP but something is dropping return traffic or SG is rejecting ephemeral ports. by default the endpoint SG was scoped to 443 only.
jen: good call. check the endpoint's security group egress rules?
alex: egress shows: allow TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 only. no ephemeral port ranges.
raj: that's the issue. Interface endpoints proxy TLS to the service, but the underlying ENI also needs ephemeral outbound allowed for related TCP sockets while service responds. our NAT path + route propagation might also be inconsistent. can we tcpdump on the app subnet ENI?
jen: running remote tcpdump now (short window).
jen: tcpdump shows SYN -> SYN/ACK from 10.0.58.21 then RST from our ENI after ~200ms.
casey: that RST is likely coming from the VPC endpoint SG or a route table misroute returning traffic to TGW without a proper path. check route table attached to the subnet where endpoint ENI lives.
alex: route tables: subnet-private-a has route 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0123 (good). but the interface endpoint ENI subnets are in the same private route table. however, I see a stale route pointing to tgw-0deadbeef for 0.0.0.0/0 in another route table (maybe leftover from the migration).
raj: ahh route propagation collision. if some AZ subnets are getting tgw default and others nat, return path symmetry breaks. we need consistent 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT for those subnets with ENIs.
jen: quick remediation: update endpoint SG egress to allow 1024-65535 TCP to 0.0.0.0/0 and remove the stray tgw default from the endpoint subnets. I can push a one-off update.
alex: doing SG change now:
```
# terraform-ish quick patch (applied manually)
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "vpce_egress_ephemeral" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 1024
  to_port     = 65535
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  security_group_id = "sg-vpce-xxxx"
}
```
jen: I removed the tgw route from the route table attached to subnet 10.0.58.0/24 and re-associated the correct private RT. pushing now.
oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-1472 for ap-southeast-1 interface ep outages. priority P2.
deploy-bot: rolling window pause applied to inference fleet in ap-southeast-1 to prevent expanded errors.
casey: re-run the healthcheck curl?
alex: retrying...
```
curl -v https://registry.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/healthcheck
* Connected to 10.0.58.21 (10.0.58.21) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
* HTTP/1.1 200 OK
* Connection #0 to host registry.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com left intact
```
alex: green. apps reporting 200s again.
jen: leaving a TODO to ensure endpoint SG defaults include ephemeral range in org policy. also add a TF guard so route propagation collisions are rejected for endpoint subnets.
raj: opened https://internal.redwood/ops/playbooks/privatelink-troubleshooting and added notes.
casey: <@alex> can you run perf tests against model loads to ensure no latent flaps?
alex: running a few qps tests for 10m, will report in channel.
alex: tests look steady. no regressions.
jen: nice. postmortem: create a small PR to our endpoint module to always add ephemeral egress + validate route table association. I'll include the policy check.
alex: ACK. closing thread once PR lands. :thumbsup:
